messages.subject: Re: MSstats installation error
messages.body_plain:
It seems that one of required package, 'data.table', can not be installed. But, we are not sure about the reason. Based on our experience, this type of installation issue can happen
(1) if you don't have full authorization in your computer, for example, the computer from company - then you should talk with IT people in your computer.
(2) conflict with some antivirus program - then pause antivirus program and try to install.

After checking two potential reason above, then could you try as below?

(1) Uninstall previous version of R through ’Control panel’ in your computer.
(2) Delete the R folder under C:/Users/xxx/Documents/ (where xxx is the user name), or under C:/Program Files/
(3) Install MSstats in Skyline (Tool > External tool > MSstats)
(4) If you still have the same error as you show,
      (4.1) Start R
      (4.2) In the console (commonly panel in the left side), could you copy these lines below and press 'Enter' key.

install.packages(c("gplots","lme4","reshape","reshape2","grid","ggplot2", "ggrepel", "minpack.lm", "data.table","Rcpp", "survival"))
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
biocLite(c("limma","marray","preprocessCore","MSnbase"))

(5) Then, install MSstats in Skyline (Tool > External tool > MSstats)

Hope that it can help your installation.

- Meena

messages.body_plain:

I recently started using Spectronaut 9 to process DIA data. Now, I would like to continue the statistical analysis in MSstats, but the dataProcess() function terminates with an error due to duplicated features. Here is a screenshot of the corresponding log file (I also attached the complete file):

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-R7Yqq2lTcKs/V43Z3SEMjNI/AAAAAAAAAKY/9KmdFPe2jVw3_5E38FvbDWmdRB9PBXajwCLcB/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2016-07-19%2Bat%2B09.38.15.png>

There is two things happening: (i) Spectronaut does not export features with censored intensities (NAs), therefor the report is incomplete. MSstats corrects this by filling up the missing lines. Interestingly, it afterwards complains about the same features being duplicated and terminates the process. Has anyone every experienced this phenomenom?

messages.subject_clean: import of Spectronaut 9 report into MSstats fails
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats support,

I meanwhile figured out where the problem was. The export scheme generated some duplicated IDs and I was able to fix this issue. Now, the dataProcess() function runs as expected and reports the right number of features and replicates in the different groups...but, the summarisation of feature intensities by Tukey's median polish fails or to be more precise it does not finish. I have been running MSstats for several hours now and there is no progress in status messages coming from dataProcess(). Interestingly, the protein was processed last is one with a high number of matched peptides (several hundred). Could it be that the median polish is not working robustly which such high numbers of features?

Greetings,
Tobi

But, It is hard to say why without seeing the data. If you can share the subset of data for that specific protein, we can investigate it.

- Meena

messages.subject: Re: subject nesting
messages.body_plain:
When you have 15 different subject IDs, the first case you mentioned, 5 different bioreplicates ID per Condition, it is nested design and MSstats considers it as group-comparison design. (Please check MSstats manual, 'assigning the values of condition, bioreplicate and run' section). MSstats used the linear model, LogIntensity ~ Group, because there is no technical replicate. therefore, (15-1)-(3-1)=12 for degree of freedom.

For the second case, it is considered as paired design with 10 different subject and MSstats used the linear model, LogIntensity ~ Group + Subject. Then, degree of freedom 14-2-8=4.

Based on your explanation about your experiment, it should be considered as paired design.

HTH.

- Meena
